selected_approach: Select Boa 0.21.1 with default features disabled inside a policy-marked non-shipped Rust executable worker. Each request creates a fresh capability-free Boa Context and crosses the WP-005 bounded JavaScriptWorkerEnvelope and four-byte length-prefixed JSON frame boundary.

Implement Ferric-owned discovery by parsing each raw player with Boa's parser, locating the combined n/signature URL-transform wrapper through structural markers, and emitting a side-effect-reduced program containing only declarations and assignment/literal expression statements from the player IIFE. Do not use regex-only discovery and do not evaluate the original full player initialization path.

Use checked-in raw site-supplied player programs plus inert provenance-bound expected observations for multiple pinned player generations. No external solver source, generated solver asset, package, executable, or runtime is imported, executed, bundled, or required.
Enforce input, output, frame, instruction, loop, recursion, stack, wall-time, job-count, age, and RSS/recycle bounds; use parent process supervision for non-cooperative timeout and cancellation.

Pin the local fforager-contracts dependency to version 0.1.0 and record one reasoned cargo-deny exception for RUSTSEC-2024-0436 because Boa 0.21.1 has no safe paste upgrade; do not carry that exception into a later product consumer without explicit re-authorization.
Emit deterministic per-case reports and an aggregate PASS_RUST_ONLY_PATH or FAILED_SPIKE_REQUIRES_OPERATOR_DECISION verdict only after dependency-independence proof passes.
rejected_options: Deno, Node.js, Bun, QuickJS, QuickJS-NG, Wasmtime, rusty_v8, Hermes, or another external/native runtime because the Operator and packet forbid them.
Nova for this spike because current maturity and corpus evidence are weaker and its unsafe GC surface adds risk without a demonstrated compatibility advantage.
Executing yt-dlp-ejs or any other yt-dlp-family solver/library asset because Ferric is an independent replacement and must own its implementation path.
Regex-only player discovery because current NewPipe source retains multiple patterns plus lexer fallback and recent releases document recurring n-function breakage.
Full raw-player evaluation because browser initialization code introduces irrelevant effects, ambient host assumptions, avoidable compatibility surface, and a larger attack/resource boundary.

Adding a second JavaScript parser such as SWC because Boa already supplies the parser required by the selected engine and a second parser would enlarge dependency and maintenance cost without closing a current acceptance gap.

Patching Boa to substitute pastey during this spike because the upstream dependency is transitive, no reviewed drop-in patch is part of Boa 0.21.1, and carrying a local engine fork would enlarge the attack and maintenance surface beyond the bounded non-shipped evidence need.
A handwritten case-specific transform table because it would echo fixture expectations rather than discover and solve real player behavior.
Network-downloading EJS/player assets during build or test because it violates deterministic offline proof and the no-build-download boundary.
Treating generic Test262 or simple eval success as YouTube challenge compatibility proof.
reuse_opportunities: Reuse the existing locked Cargo workspace, architecture policy, report envelope, scanner, negative-fixture harness, and canonical gates.
Reuse WP-005 JavaScriptWorkerEnvelope, FrameDecoder, ProtocolLimits, typed failure codes, cancellation generations, and state-machine identities.
Reuse WP-004 stable corpus identities, deterministic normalization, and optional external-comparison provenance without reusing external implementation code.
Reuse Rust std process, pipe, timing, hashing, and filesystem APIs plus already-approved serde/serde_json/sha2 before adding any new mechanism.
basis.validation_plan: Run the committed raw-player corpus through the spawned Rust worker; inspect reports; run malformed/partial/oversized/protocol/cancel/timeout/crash/memory/capability/cache/context/recycle/quarantine probes; mutate an expected output and prove the same aggregate oracle rejects it; scan dependency, source, executable assets, build scripts, artifacts, process plans, FFI, links, and downloads; prove canonical build/test/verification succeeds with yt-dlp absent; run format/check/test/doc/Clippy/architecture/deep/PR gates; then perform two independent adversarial reviews through engine-security/resource-isolation and corpus-proof/contract-integrity lenses.

assumptions: Pinned external observations may remain comparison provenance, but Ferric-owned specifications and committed corpora are canonical and no external implementation code is an executable packet input.
A passing spike selects a prerequisite mechanism only and is not a video downloader or product capability.
The logged-in Firefox session is optional live-canary context and is never a source of committed cookies, tokens, secrets, or deterministic corpus truth.
non_goals: Downloading the requested Short, implementing the YouTube extractor, or claiming full YouTube support.
Shipping the worker or granting it network/filesystem/process capabilities.
Adding an external runtime, Python, yt-dlp or companion implementation dependency, executable solver asset, Wasm, or a new native dependency.

corpus_contract.oracle_identity: Ferric-owned YouTube challenge corpus; optional external comparison observations carry separate pinned provenance
corpus_contract.mandatory_cases: Every pinned case in the checked-in WP-006 manifest binds raw site-player bytes, variant, challenge type, input, inert expected observation, and provenance without bundling or executing external solver code.
corpus_contract.pass_threshold: 100 percent exact output agreement for mandatory deterministic cases, with no skipped or structurally-only cases.
corpus_contract.live_canary_policy: Optional, non-blocking, separately labeled, sanitized, and never allowed to replace deterministic corpus proof.
corpus_contract.failure_bundle: Case ID, upstream identities, script/player hashes, engine identity, bounded non-secret input, expected and observed result, typed error, limits, duration, process/RSS observation, and replay command.

resource_and_security_contract.capabilities: No registered network, filesystem, environment, process, dynamic import, module loader, console, timer, or secret-bearing host functions.
resource_and_security_contract.isolation: The selected Rust engine creates a fresh capability-free execution context per job; host-owned content-addressed prepared-program artifacts do not retain JavaScript heap or global state across jobs.
resource_and_security_contract.termination: Engine budgets are cooperative first-line controls; parent wall deadline/cancellation may terminate and reap the separate worker. Timeout is a bounded policy outcome, not proof that arbitrary code could never finish.
resource_and_security_contract.memory: Input/output and engine structural limits are exact; parent RSS supervision provides bounded detection and forced worker termination. The report must state OS hard-containment coverage and residual race/overshoot rather than claim a perfect in-engine heap cap.

minimum_controls: Ferric-owned discovery and solving execute against raw pinned player bytes through the Rust worker, an output mutation fails the same acceptance path, and a bundled yt-dlp-family solver asset is rejected.
Every worker request crosses the bounded public frame/envelope boundary and receives a correlated typed terminal outcome.
Parent supervision proves termination and reap for infinite loop, cancellation, crash, malformed stream, timeout, and memory pressure.
Dependency and source scans reject all forbidden runtimes, downloads, FFI, native links, and indirect wrappers.
No PASS is possible with skipped mandatory cases, missing process proof, structural-only behavioral evidence, or a positive product-progress claim.

Implement typed report/verdict generation and capability, bounds, lifecycle, cache, churn, dependency, and counterfactual probes.
Run multi-lens independent adversarial reviews, remediate every confirmed finding, simplify, and rerun all acceptance and canonical gates.
